meta.program: Proposition 123 Land Banking (Affordable Housing Financing Fund)
meta.administrator: CHFA, on behalf of the Colorado Office of Economic Development and International Trade (OEDIT)
meta.program_quote: The Land Banking program provides grants to eligible local or tribal governments and forgivable loans to eligible nonprofits with a demonstrated history of providing affordable housing. These funds must be used to acquire and preserve land for affordable for-sale housing or affordable rental housing.
meta.eligibility_quote: To be eligible, affordable housing projects seeking support from the Affordable Housing Financing Fund must be located in a jurisdiction that has completed a Proposition 123 Local Government Affordable Housing Commitment with the Colorado Department of Local Affairs − Division of Housing.

open_round.summary: Projects in rural and resort areas can apply now, until December 31, 2026 or until the money runs out. Projects anywhere in Colorado can apply from January 2027. About $31 million is available this year.
open_round.quote: CHFA will accept applications for the Proposition 123 Land Banking program for projects located in Rural and Rural Resort communities* beginning September 15, 2026, and continuing through December 31, 2026, or until funds are exhausted. Beginning January 2027, applications will be accepted for all projects, including those not located in Rural or Rural Resort communities.
open_round.allocation_quote: The FY27 total Land Banking allocation will be approximately $31 million.

meta.location_note: CHFA lists a town for each award, not an address. Each pin sits at the Census 2024 Gazetteer centre of that town; an award that lists several towns has a pin in each.
meta.units_note: Units are the estimate in each award list; land banking buys land, and the homes come later.

since.text: The site is 1130 and 1138 18 1/2 Road in Fruita. CHFA committed the grant on May 16, 2025, and the city closed on the land in November 2025. The city says it plans mostly entry-level single-family homes for sale, with some apartments. Under the grant, the homes must be permitted and their construction loan closed within ten years of the land purchase.
since.quote: for the acquisition of land for the development of The Fruita Commons, located at 1138 18 1/2 Rd. and 1130 18 1/2 Rd., Fruita, Mesa County, CO, 81521 ... Within 10 years of the Closing (“Final Deadline”), the Project must obtain all necessary permits, and the construction loan for the Project must be closed and funded ... we closed on the purchase of the Fruita Commons property in the northeast part of Fruita ... The focus of the property will be to provide entry-level single-family detached workforce housing units for sale, with some multifamily units as well.
